title: Maximize Score After Pair Deletions
summary: Given an array of integers nums, repeatedly perform one of the following operations while the array has more than two elements: - Remove the first two elements and add their sum to the score.
statement: Given an array of integers nums, repeatedly perform one of the following operations while the array has more than two elements: - Remove the first two elements and add their sum to the score. - Remove the last two elements and add their sum to the score. - Remove the first and last element and add their sum to the score. Continue this process until only two elements remain in the array. Return the maximum score achievable by following these operations.
constraints: nums has at least three integers.
While more than two remain, remove either the first two, last two, or first and last, adding their sum.
Maximize the total score; an odd-length array ends with one element and an even-length array ends with two.
hints: Every operation scores removed values, so maximizing score is minimizing the sum left at termination.
For odd length any single value can remain; for even length the two survivors must be adjacent in the original order.
Subtract the minimum element for odd n, or the minimum adjacent-pair sum for even n, from the total.
Endpoint deletions can expose any chosen valid survivor set, while crossing survivors cannot become the final adjacent pair.
editorial: Endpoint deletions can expose any chosen valid survivor set, while crossing survivors cannot become the final adjacent pair.

tests.explanation: Remove the first two values to score six, leaving one.
The maximum score equals the total minus the minimum adjacent pair that can remain.
